title: Redesign Library for visual discovery, organization and AI reuse
body:
Make Library a compact visual browser for large component collections: find useful components, understand their appearance and purpose, then direct the AI to use them.

Acceptance:
- Dense thumbnail list plus optional grid; search names/descriptions/tags/use cases; type/compatibility/favorite/in-scene filters.
- Shallow folders, tags and favorites; later saved collections.
- Details lead with previews, purpose, use cases, inputs/output and examples. Code/history stay secondary. Narrow details use Back; wide layout shows results beside details.
- Single/multiple component selection attaches stable references to an AI request, or honestly offers Copy request until attachment exists.
- Explicit isolated demos for sources, effects and non-image components; one active demo; preserve current scene and release resources.
- Preserve catalogs, IDs, revisions, source/history and linked scenes; independent actual-app UX review.

Delivery: browser/discovery/details/AI reuse first, then demos and saved collections. Reuse LUX-164 clipping work.
Full approved design and safety/acceptance detail: artifacts/library-organization-brief.md, Approved redesign detail — 17 September 2026.
Planning only; no dispatch.
reason: Expand existing Library feature with user-approved compact visual browser, AI selection and isolated demo design; preserve existing work and assignment.
